_doc: ears-mail's wake rules, SHIPPED with no seats: a fresh install calls nobody by name until a seat is added, and every finished turn is still mailed to its device (--to device). Seats live in the USER file ~/.sessionkit/voice/settings/wake.json, written by: ears wake add SEAT [--names 'a|b']; never edit this file (ears wake refuses it). keeper/defaults/wake.example.json shows a filled-in file. Defaults, then each seat's own; a seat's names and openers are regex alternations, and its names default to its key. 'a' left the default openers ("a Bob thing" is no call); a seat can add it back. A seat's key is its address's local part, WHOLE: the device mail's Ears-Rule writes KEY@host=call and the pager matches it exactly, so sessionmail@host1=call does not wake sessionmail+engineer. 'again' lists the say-again phrases: a turn that is WHOLLY one (names, openers and 'sorry'/'please' stripped from its ends) replays the newest heard line of the seat it names, else of whoever spoke last, within again_window seconds, and wakes nobody; [] or false turns it off for a seat.
